criteria.text: Identifies that Section 2.2 of the Distribution Agreement renews the agreement automatically for successive five-year terms unless non-renewal notice is given no more than 270 and no fewer than 240 days before expiry. Calculates that window against the June 30, 2027 expiry as roughly early October to about November 2, 2026. Explains that missing it locks Halvorsen in, with its purchase commitments, until 2032. Recommends serving notice, or deciding on and negotiating an amendment, before the window closes.

Identifies that Section 5.3 of the Distribution Agreement gives Halvorsen 30 days from receipt of a price adjustment notice to object or remove products, failing which the increase is deemed accepted. Notes that the Price Adjustment Notice (a 14% increase effective November 1, 2026) was received on August 21, 2026, so the objection deadline was on or about September 20, 2026. States that the objection right has lapsed or is very likely lapsed, so Halvorsen is limited to negotiating a concession, or must confirm with the client whether a timely objection was sent.

Identifies that Halvorsen's indemnity in Section 11.1 of the Distribution Agreement is broad enough to cover claims caused by Brightmere, such as product defect claims, and that Section 12.3(a) excludes it from the liability cap, while Brightmere's indemnity under Section 11.2 remains capped. Explains that this leaves Halvorsen with one-sided, unlimited exposure. Recommends narrowing the indemnity to Halvorsen's own fault and/or making it mutual or capped.

Identifies that Section 3 of the First Amendment deletes and replaces Section 12.3 of the Distribution Agreement and drops the carve-out for Brightmere's recall cost reimbursement under Section 9. Explains that Brightmere's recall reimbursement is therefore now limited by the 12-month fees cap, which a large recall could exceed. Recommends reinstating the recall carve-out.

Identifies that Section 6 of the First Amendment makes the agreement as amended subject to Delaware law and exclusive jurisdiction in Wilmington, Delaware. Explains that this conflicts with the New York law and New York County forum in Sections 17.1 and 17.2 of the Distribution Agreement, and that the amendment prevails under the order of precedence. Recommends conforming the governing law and forum back to New York.
States that the Price Adjustment Notice was received on August 21, 2026.
States that the initial term of the Distribution Agreement ends June 30, 2027.
States that under Section 1.4 of the Distribution Agreement, written amendments take precedence over the body of the Agreement.
Is structured as a memo to the supervising partner. For each issue, it gives the document and section where the issue appears, why it matters for Halvorsen, and a recommended fix.
Does not conclude that Brightmere's recall cost reimbursement remains outside the liability cap after the First Amendment.
Does not conclude that the agreement as amended remains governed by New York law with a New York forum, without acknowledging the Delaware provisions in the First Amendment.
